slot.brief: Give log(x/m) vs log P data/plot; extract the slope and intercept, state what slope = 1 means, and interpret adsorption behaviour — includes a subtle point about saturation limiting the isotherm.

stem: For the Freundlich isotherm, $\log\dfrac{x}{m}=\log k+\dfrac{1}{n}\log P$. Common-log data give $(\log P,\log(x/m))=(0,-1)$ and $(1,0)$. Which interpretation is correct?
options: $n=1$, $k=0.1$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$; the model predicts a finite saturation plateau at high $P$.
$n=1$, $k=10$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=10P$; the model has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.
$n=1$, $k=0.1$, and $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$; the model has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.

verdicts.working: The slope is 1/n = (0 - (-1))/(1 - 0) = 1, so n = 1. The intercept is log k = -1, so k = 0.1. Thus x/m = 0.1P, which has no finite saturation plateau.

working:
$\text{slope}=\dfrac{0-(-1)}{1-0}=1=\dfrac{1}{n}\Rightarrow n=1$
$\text{intercept}=\log k=-1\Rightarrow k=0.1$
$\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$; Freundlich does not include a saturation limit.

Independent check: The slope is 1/n = (0 - (-1))/(1 - 0) = 1, so n = 1. The intercept is log k = -1, so k = 0.1. Thus x/m = 0.1P, which has no finite saturation plateau.
solution:
The slope is $1/n$, and the intercept is $\log k$:
$$\frac{1}{n}=\frac{0-(-1)}{1-0}=1,\qquad \log k=-1$$
Hence $n=1$, $k=0.1$, so $\dfrac{x}{m}=0.1P$. The Freundlich isotherm has no finite saturation plateau and must fail at sufficiently high $P$.
